item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Revoking permanent residencies would take 'eight years', hundreds of unresolved shootings after gang war, property prices rose in February and other news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: Work permits, Mello and marzipan: What changes in Sweden in March 2026
item.description: Parliament will vote on hiking the minimum salary for a work permit and Sweden's Eurovision contender will be chosen. Here's what happens in Sweden in March.

item.title: NEW: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: Sweden's Migration Agency: Revoking permanent residency could take 'eight years'
item.description: If the government decides to go through with a proposal to convert permanent residence permits into temporary permits, the Migration Agency predicts that processing all cases would take eight years.

item.title: TELL US: Which are the best districts for foreigners in Gothenburg?
item.description: From Majorna, with its cafés and boutiques, to suburbs like Eriksberg, Kålltorp and Mölndal, people living in Gothenburg are spoiled for choice. We want to hear from readers about which district is best for foreigners.

item.title: Can this campaign group change the Swedish government's mind on citizenship?
item.description: Sweden's government recently announced plans to tighten up citizenship rules for all applications from June 6th – even those already in the queue. The Local spoke to Patrick Gallen, spokesperson for Fair Transition, a campaign group calling for transitional rules in the new law.

item.title: HOOONNNK! What's that noise? No need to freak out, Sweden
item.description: Don't be alarmed if you hear a long, deafening siren on Monday afternoon in Sweden. It is just 'Hoarse Fredrik' – or 'Hesa Fredrik' – and it is only a test.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: älskling
item.description: When you add a -ling to love, like dear in darling.

item.title: Swedish parliament committee set to debate proposal to halt teen deportations
item.description: A Swedish parliament committee is on Tuesday expected to reject a proposal to freeze deportations of young adults.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Unemployed graduates on the rise as companies want blue-collar workers, no planned evacuation flights to Sweden from UAE, committee set to debate teen deportation proposal and more news from Sweden on Tuesday.
